transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’ve just been feeling really low. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I can’t seem to shake this heavy, hopeless feeling. It’s like everything I tried to build back up after my divorce has kind of collapsed, and I’m just… sitting under it. Does that make sense?
How long have you been feeling this heavy, hopeless feeling?

Um… I think it’s been about a month now. It kind of started around when the financial stuff after the divorce got really messy. I kept telling myself it was just stress and that I’d bounce back, but… it’s been hanging over me since then, I guess.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I haven’t really been doing much, but I don’t know if it’s that I’ve lost interest exactly or if I’m just… tired and overwhelmed. The things I used to like don’t sound as appealing lately, I guess, but maybe that’s normal with stress?
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in?

Um… I wish I had a better answer. I can’t really think of anything that feels genuinely enjoyable right now. Maybe little things are okay in the moment, like a show being on in the background, but I don’t know if I’d call it pleasure exactly. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from things that normally would bring you happiness?

I… I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but things that usually make me happy just feel kind of flat lately. Like I can recognize that they should be nice, but I don’t really feel much from them. Is that what you mean?
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself?

I… I don’t want to worry anyone, and I’m not saying I have some big plan or anything, but… yeah. I’ve had thoughts like it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. It got pretty intense at one point, enough that I scared myself and called the employee assistance program. Is that okay to say? I mean… that’s what happened.
Have you noticed any change in your weight recently?
Um… I don’t think so? I haven’t really been keeping close track, to be honest. My clothes seem about the same, I think. If it’s important I can start checking, but I haven’t noticed a big change.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly or feeling restless and unable to sit still lately?

Yeah… maybe more on the restless side. I wouldn’t say I was just, you know, wildly out of control or anything, but I did start pushing myself into extra proposals at work and calling colleagues with new ideas. I was volunteering for tasks nobody had really asked me to take on.

And then when there wasn’t anything useful left to do, I’d just pace around my apartment. I kept telling myself it was just being productive, but… I guess it was a lot. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you had any days in the past month where you felt somewhat better, or has it been consistently bad?

There have been maybe little moments where I can function or seem okay, but honestly… it’s mostly been bad. That’s kind of why I came in. I just can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling, like everything I built after the divorce has collapsed and I’m just sitting under it.

I’m sorry, that sounds dramatic. I just… that’s what it feels like.
Can you think of any activity that you used to enjoy and still find pleasure in, no matter how small?

I’m not sure… I wish I had a better answer. I’ve been trying to think of something small, but nothing really comes to mind in a reliable way. Maybe there are moments where I’m distracted enough that it’s not awful, but I don’t know if I’d call it pleasure.

Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
Can you think of any time recently when you felt even slight pleasure from something?

I’m trying to think of one… I don’t want to say “no” too quickly if that’s not fair. Maybe a cup of coffee tasted okay, or I watched something and didn’t hate it for a few minutes, but I don’t know if that was pleasure exactly.

So… I guess I haven’t really noticed anything that felt like actual enjoyment lately. Is that an okay way to answer?
Have you felt a lack of pleasure in things you used to enjoy for most of the day, nearly every day, over the past month?

I’m not totally sure how to measure “most of the day,” but… yes, I think that’s probably fair. I don’t want to overstate it, but things I used to like just don’t really feel good anymore, and that’s been true pretty much day after day lately.

Is that the kind of answer you’re looking for?
Have you had any days in the past two weeks where you felt normal or nearly normal?

Not really, I don’t think so. I mean… there may have been little stretches where I seemed more okay, but I wouldn’t say I felt normal or even nearly normal.

It’s been about two weeks of this kind of… out-of-control swing, like being really wired and then just crashing. I’m sorry if that’s not a clean answer, but no, I don’t think I’ve had a normal day in there.
Have you had any significant difficulty with concentration or making decisions over the past month?

Yes… I mean, I’ve been trying not to make too big a deal of it, but it has been pretty bad.

At work I’ll look at a basic drainage calculation, or even a spreadsheet I’ve used for years, and my mind just sort of blanks. I sit there rereading the same numbers over and over, and then I don’t trust myself to make even a normal decision from it.

I know that probably sounds concerning. I’m usually better than that. Is that the kind of concentration difficulty you mean?
Have you felt sad or empty most of the day?

Yes… I think so.

I’ve been trying to tell myself it’s just stress and that I should be handling it better, but honestly I came in because I can’t shake this really heavy, hopeless feeling. It feels like everything I built back up after the divorce has just… collapsed, and I’m sitting underneath it.

Sorry, that sounds dramatic. But yes, sad or empty most of the day is probably accurate.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy most of the time?

I’m… not totally sure how to answer that.

I don’t think I’ve been paying close enough attention to what I’m enjoying versus just getting through the day. I guess I haven’t really felt like myself, but I don’t want to overstate it if that’s not exactly the same thing.

Do you mean like hobbies, or wanting to see people, that kind of thing?
How many weeks have you been feeling this way?

I think… about four weeks? Maybe right around a month.

It started hanging over me after the financial mess from the divorce got worse. I kept thinking I’d shake it off once I got things organized, but it hasn’t really lifted. Does that timeline make sense for what you’re asking?
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over the past month?

I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t been tracking it or anything.

My clothes maybe feel a little different, but I don’t know if it’s enough to call it significant. I’m sorry, I know that’s not a very precise answer. Should I have weighed myself before coming in?
Have you felt a lack of pleasure in almost all activities for most of every day over the past two weeks?

I’m not sure I’d say almost all activities, or most of every day… I don’t know if I can answer that cleanly.

I haven’t been noticing pleasure very much, but I also haven’t really been checking in with myself that way. I don’t want to exaggerate and say “yes” if it’s not exactly true. Maybe things just feel kind of muted? Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have you had any days in the past month where you felt no sadness or hopelessness at all?

I… honestly, I don’t think so. I wish I could say there were days where it totally lifted, but it’s been kind of there all the time.

That’s why I came in, really. I can’t seem to shake this heavy, hopeless feeling—like everything I built after the divorce has collapsed, and I’m just sitting under it. I’m sorry if that sounds dramatic, but… that’s the closest way I can describe it.
